messages:
jen: Heads-up — noticed a weird chart in the latency dashboard after the canary rolled weights up at 09:03 UTC. p50 jumped ~40ms while p95/p99 actually dropped a bit. looks inverted :thinking_face:

sanjay: Huh. Do we have the query that powers that panel? p50 up while tails down is unusual unless sample sets changed.

jen: Panel uses the standard rollup: `approx_percentiles(duration_ms, [50,95,99])` over 1m windows, rollup mode=tdigest. Query id: ui-rlatency-endpoint-203.

lee: Could be sampling origin change — if the canary routed more short requests to variant B (fast path) and long requests stayed on A, p95 could drop while median moves if sample counts shift. But that usually moves tails same direction.

sam: Another guess: smoothing/window aligned with allocation change. We have a 3-min decaying window on p50 display but tails use raw bucket percentiles for p95/p99. Dashboard mixes two aggregation strategies atm.

jen: Wait that's interesting — I remember a recent PR that set `display_mode=smoothed` only for p50 to reduce jitter. maybe that made medians less sensitive to tail routing.

sanjay: Can we run the backend query without smoothing and compare? something like:
```
SELECT agg_tdigest(percentile=50) as p50_raw, agg_tdigest(percentile=95) as p95_raw, count(*)
FROM telemetry.rollups
WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND ts BETWEEN 1680000000 AND 1680000060
GROUP BY 1m
```

lee: I'll run a tight timebox around the 09:03 change and dump per-route counts. If the denominator shifted (more small requests from mobile), that explains median jump.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout update: variant B weight increased 20% -> 40% at 2025-03-12T09:03:24Z (trigger: auto-scale policy).

sam: That matches. Also check kvcache hit rate — small prompt cached responses are very quick. If B had a higher cache hit, median could skew down or up depending which side moved.

jen: I pulled raw samples for that minute. Counts per variant: A=850, B=1100. p50_A=220ms, p50_B=180ms. But global p50 went to 240ms. hmm.

lee: Did you weight-merge percentiles naively? If the UI computes global p50 by blending per-variant p50s equally instead of population-weighted, a higher weight on the slower variant could move the shown p50 opposite to raw tail behavior.

sanjay: Exactly — bug hypothesis: the frontend was recently changed to average percentiles across cohorts for chart smoothing. That produces nonsense: mean(p50_A,p50_B) != p50_global unless weights applied.

jen: omg we shipped an averaging step. @sam can you revert the smoothing for percentile aggregation? That must be the root cause.

sam: On it. Reverting the UI smoothing flag for percentile panels now. I'll also add a note to the console docs that percentiles must be recombined by population-weighted tdigest merge, not arithmetic mean.

lee: After revert, also validate with an exact merge of tdigest rollups to show population-weighted p50/p95/p99 for that minute. If that matches raw per-request percentile, we're golden.

deploy-bot: Revert PR deployed to staging at 09:18 UTC.

jen: Post-revert: dashboard p50 moved back in line with tails. Thanks team. Action items: sam add a UI check to forbid arithmetic averaging of percentiles, sanjay add a linter to catch smoothing-mode mismatches, lee generate a small runbook for debugging percentile anomalies.

sanjay: I'll draft the linter rule. quick note: add tests that validate merging semantics with synthetic cohorts of different sizes.

sam: Will follow up with a small patch & unit tests. Sorry for the noise :grimacing:
